motions.motion: approve the Conditional Use Permit for Weyburn Retreat subject to the following: Conditions: 1. A Shared Maintenance Agreement shall be entered into between the HOAs of both projects. 2. All exterior lighting shall be downlit and night sky compliant. 3. The Salt Lake City water provider issue a will serve letter. 4. Professional designers shall be employed for architecture and landscaping. 5. The new drawings presented at this meeting shall be adopted. 6. There shall be a 15-foot radius cut around the box. TRC Findings: 1. The use is consistent with the city’s general plan and the zone in which it is located. City of Holladay Planning Commission Meeting - 05/19/2020 4 2. The use is compatible with the land use character in the immediate area. 3. Provides a more affordable housing alternative to single-family development in a time of dramatic housing shortages locally and regionally. 4. Enhances property values in the area as it replaces underutilized institutional use, contrasts with older development to the east, and dovetails with existing similarly zoned recent development immediately to the south. 5. Will result in minimal traffic impact on (no through traffic) on adjacent residential neighborhoods. 6. Will have minimal impact on adjacent public streets, 1300 E and Spring Lane. 7. The PUD as proposed complies with the allowance for this amount and type of development in the R-M zone. No more than 16 total dwellings; 8 twin-homes will be allowed. 8. The height of the dwellings complies with the R-M zone. Height will not exceed 30 feet as defined by City ordinance. 9. The buildings are no more than two stories abutting Tobermory. 10. Buildings meet or exceed the minimum 20-foot setback for development on corner properties from both Spring Lane and 1300 East. 11. Improves pedestrian access. 12. Preserves vegetation and open space and minimizes impact on the slopes and will add new tree canopy to the community. 13. Vehicular access to the site (ingress/egress plan) is in line with the recommendations of the City’s professional transportation consultant, Dr. Joe Perrin, (Traffic study on file) regarding capacity and safety including: a. Tobermory Lane as proposed by the applicant will be widened by 2 feet for each travel lane; (see attached graphic). This will provide a total of 22 feet of right-of-way width with 20 feet drivable instead of 16 feet currently. (See attached graphic). b. Adding a stripe to the middle of Tobermory lane as recommended by Dr. Perrin. c. Installation of a four-foot-wide sidewalk from Weyburn Lane to Spring Lane for use of all residents of both Tobermory Ridge and Weyburn City of Holladay Planning Commission Meeting - 05/19/2020 5 with the applicant granting access across private property for the general public to use and enjoy. (See attached graphic). 14. The architecture (See attached color graphics) is attractive and in character with other PUDs in Holladay. In response to a question about the radius, Commissioner Layton explained that currently, the radius is 15 feet from Spring Lane and Tobermory Way. A 25-foot radius would broaden the shape of the arc, which would extend across the utilities. He commented that 25 feet is a very broad turning radius for a small street. By comparison, it was noted that the radius into Weyburn is 28 feet. Sidewalk continuity and safety issues were discussed

approve the Conceptual Site Plan and Building Design for The Apollo at 2240-2254 East Murray Holladay Road. The public hearing was left open through preliminary approval based on the following: Findings: 1. The building location and architecture has been approved. 2. Site development details are compatible with the vision and standards of the Holladay Village. 3. Subject to the project being serviced by all life safety utilities and further examination and discussion on the proposed parking plan. 4. Safe, predictable traffic patterns are proposed. The following areas to be highlighted at preliminary plat review: 1. Programming for tandem stalls. 2. Dedication of Murray Holladay Road. 3. Public amenity - consider art installation on the blank wall behind the billboard. 4. Clarified plan for the design of off-street stalls. 5. Public art installation to be determined later.
